name: Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6)
description: The six-item K6 for nonspecific psychological distress over the past 30 days, preserved with its standard response scale and scoring metadata.
source: Kessler et al. (2003), Screening for serious mental illness in the general population. Instrument obtained from the National Comorbidity Survey.
license: Free to use without formal permission; citation and copyright notice required. Copyright © Ronald C. Kessler, PhD.
intended_use: Brief assessment of nonspecific psychological distress in adolescent or adult research. It is not a diagnostic instrument and is not a momentary EMA measure.
validation_status: Established instrument. Preserve the original 30-day timeframe and response coding when using validated scoring; evaluate appropriateness for the intended population and language.

measure.instrument: Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6), self-administered English
measure.scoring: Code None of the time=0, A little of the time=1, Some of the time=2, Most of the time=3, All of the time=4; sum six items for a 0–24 score. Follow the cited source for interpretation.

references.label: National Comorbidity Survey — K6/K10 scales, permissions, and scoring
references.note: Author-maintained instrument, permission, translations, and scoring information.

references.label: Kessler et al. (2003), Archives of General Psychiatry
references.note: Development and validation citation requested by the instrument author.

questions.text: During the past 30 days, about how often did you feel nervous?
During the past 30 days, about how often did you feel hopeless?
During the past 30 days, about how often did you feel restless or fidgety?
During the past 30 days, about how often did you feel so depressed that nothing could cheer you up?
During the past 30 days, about how often did you feel that everything was an effort?
During the past 30 days, about how often did you feel worthless?
